name: Maaseiah
title: The Priest Who Supported the Reformation
summary: Maaseiah is a name that appears several times in the Old Testament and refers to different individuals. The most prominent Maaseiah was a priest who actively participated in Ezra's reforms after returning from exile in Babylon, and who was among those who had taken foreign wives and had to send them away. The name means 'work of the Lord' and is borne by several priests, Levites, and leaders in Israel.

keyEvents.title: Among the Priests Who Had Taken Foreign Wives
keyEvents.description: Maaseiah was one of the priests who had married women from the surrounding peoples and had to commit to sending them away as part of Ezra's reform.

keyEvents.title: Participation in the Reading of the Law
keyEvents.description: A Maaseiah stood at Ezra's right hand when he read the law to the people by the Water Gate, which showed his prominent position among the people.

keyEvents.title: Contribution to the Dedication of the Wall
keyEvents.description: Maaseiah participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah's leadership, a significant event for the rebuilt community.

keyEvents.title: Father of Seraiah and grandfather of Baruch
keyEvents.description: In the book of Jeremiah, a Maaseiah is mentioned as the father of Neriah and grandfather of Baruch, to whom Jeremiah wrote, and of Seraiah, who was tasked with delivering a message to Babylon.

keyEvents.title: Temple guard during Jeremiah's time
keyEvents.description: Maaseiah, son of Shallum, served as a gatekeeper in the temple and played a prominent role as a priest in Jerusalem during the prophet Jeremiah's time.

keyEvents.title: Governor of Jerusalem during Josiah's reforms
keyEvents.description: A Maaseiah served as the city governor in Jerusalem during King Josiah's religious reforms and contributed to restoring proper worship.
